title: Loss, certainty and the last feeling
header_line: My analysis of one book on negotiation. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What would they lose if there is no deal?
I said that the chapter covers the certainty effect and loss aversion. The book says you must persuade them that they have something concrete to lose if the deal falls through.
A student said that people do not want to take a risk on buying something because of the fear of loss, even though the benefits sound very good.
I gave an example from my field: you walk a shoreline with the customer and show what is receding, so the loss is concrete and in front of them.
I said you can label: it seems like you are the kind of person who does not want to hurt anyone, and then you wait for the silence, the stuttering, the reaction.
A student said that in a rebrand, you anchor the final phase, the feeling of when it is all done, because it is a lot about how people perceive their brand.

I said that independence and the freedom of choice are what a person on a call about their job is really looking for, and that people drive themselves with compulsive thinking. This is general, with the person left out.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write what your customer loses if they do nothing.
Write how you will show it concretely.
Write the label for their fear.
Write the feeling you want at the end.
Write the silence you will wait for.

check.q: What did I say the book says to persuade them of?
choices: That they have something concrete to lose

check.q: What did a student say people fear?
What did a student say to anchor?

recap: Make the loss concrete. Label the fear. Anchor the ending.
